scope: Independent read-only audit of delivered version 0 GIF and official 2022 Telegram promotional MP4; no current native-client verification
frame_numbering: All n here are zero-based; source PTS = n/60. Earlier supplied evidence uses one-based PNG numbers.

source.cadence: 569 PTS gaps alternate rounded 16666/16667 microseconds, consistent with 1/60 s

delivered_v0_gif.capture_type: Deterministic offline sampling of shared JavaScript runtime, not browser screen recording

first.limitations: First reveal includes changing bubble/media framing and slight residual scaling. Approximate similarity registration used for detail thresholds. Before enough photo appears, alignment is underconstrained. Promotional time-remapping cannot be excluded.

second.limitations: Tutorial ring overlaps image and fades through late reveal; exact terminal native-mask frame cannot be isolated. 180 ms is a reasonable approximation for this particular stationary segment, not a measured universal Telegram constant.

conclusions: No evidence of an encoding time-scale bug: delivered GIF delays total exactly the declared 3.600 s; 30/40 ms cadence is valid GIF centisecond quantization of 30 fps.

30 fps export loses the weak initial ramp: click aligns to a fully hidden sample and next sample occurs 33.333 ms later. Five visible intermediate samples make a short reveal look abrupt compared with source 60 fps.

Practically all recovered detail is visible by GIF 1.430 s, only 100 ms after first revealing frame; runtime terminal state is later. Nominal 180 ms should not be described as 180 ms of equally visible change.
First and second reveal segments in the official 2022 promotional video have different observed visible durations; the second alone underlies the existing 180 ms target.
White tutorial ring starts roughly 0.42 s before second reveal and must not be counted as product reveal duration.
GIF auto-loop and hard reset are preview choreography, not evidence of native Telegram behavior; hard reset may add a snap to the overall impression.
Neither this promotional MP4 nor the offline renderer verifies current native Telegram speed or actual browser playback scheduling.

pixel_method.description: Inspect native-frame crop contact sheets. Quantify photo-detail recovery by high-pass RGB regression against fully clear reference (Gaussian sigma5px), using 8px local aggregation and textured-pixel threshold. Cross-check full media against tutorial-annulus-excluded results. Register first reveal with small similarity transform because its presentation framing moves. Threshold intervals intentionally span sample uncertainty and metric variation. These are approximate recovered-photo-detail fractions, not literal percentage of native mask area or renderer alpha.
pixel_method.caution: Unregistered first-reveal regression and annulus-excluded global means alone bias midpoint timing; use summary intervals backed by registered/full-crop and visual checks.

publicBundleNote: Historical numeric audit, retained without original video, pixel crops, comparison media or version 0 GIF. These source measurements were not repeated for the public release.
